universal_advance_gate.description: Applies to every code phase across all project types before the phase is marked complete.
universal_advance_gate.exempt_reason: Phase 0 and D produce documents only. Phase 7 captures learnings. Phases 8, 11-16 are human-owned QA, infra, legal, and launch steps with no new code deliverables.
universal_advance_gate.criterion: Run /phase-audit. Address critical findings (dead code, broken conventions) before advancing. Defer acceptable shortcuts with a ponytail: comment. Attach the score line to the phase sign-off.

description: Full-stack web application — server-rendered or SPA frontend with a backend API, database, authentication, and deployment pipeline.

phases.name: Planning & DDD
phases.purpose: Phase 0 is a collaborative working session — not a deliverable Claude produces alone. Claude facilitates each activity by asking questions and capturing the human's answers. Every artifact must be reviewed and explicitly confirmed by the human before Phase 0 can advance. None of these documents is 'done' until the human says so.

deliverables.text: design/kano.md — Features classified as Must-be, One-dimensional, Attractive, Indifferent, or Reverse. Claude proposes candidates from the product story; human classifies each one. Scope decisions (v1 vs deferred) made for every Attractive feature. Scope: slice-scoped — if the product is multi-module, cover only the modules of the declared first slice (.workbench/slice.json); inventing for modules with no customer is fabrication, not planning.

design/task-flow.md — Step-by-step sequences for each core user task (from Must-be + One-dimensional features). Human describes what the user does; Claude captures and asks about branches and failure states. Scope: slice-scoped — if the product is multi-module, cover only the modules of the declared first slice (.workbench/slice.json); inventing for modules with no customer is fabrication, not planning.

design/user-flow.md — Screen-by-screen navigation map with auth gates, empty states, and error states. Mermaid diagram. Screen names must come from the human — they become ubiquitous language. Scope: slice-scoped — if the product is multi-module, cover only the modules of the declared first slice (.workbench/slice.json); inventing for modules with no customer is fabrication, not planning.
design/event-storm.md — All domain events in temporal order (what changes state in the system). Human drives domain knowledge; Claude facilitates and captures.
design/bounded-contexts.md — Named bounded contexts with ownership boundaries, aggregate roots, and their invariants.
design/glossary.md — Ubiquitous language: every domain term defined and used consistently from this point forward across code, docs, and conversation.
docs/product-development/product-story.md — initial product story: target user, problem being solved, and core value proposition. Seeded to project RAG.

advance_criteria: Human has reviewed design/kano.md and confirmed all feature classifications and scope decisions — no unresolved items
Human has reviewed design/task-flow.md and confirmed all task steps, branches, and failure states match their intent
Human has reviewed design/user-flow.md and confirmed all screens are named and all navigation paths are correct
Human has reviewed design/event-storm.md and confirmed all domain events are captured in sequence
Bounded contexts named, owned, and boundaries explicitly agreed
design/glossary.md complete — every term used in the above documents is defined
Human explicitly says 'approve phase 0' or equivalent confirmation

phases.name: Scaffold
phases.purpose: Establish the project structure, tooling, and CI baseline before any feature work. A clean scaffold means features can be added without structural debt.
deliverables: Framework chosen and initialized (Next.js, Remix, SvelteKit, or equivalent)
TypeScript configured (strict mode)
Linting and formatting set up (ESLint, Prettier)
Environment variable structure documented in .env.example
Database connection verified (local dev database running)
CI pipeline defined (GitHub Actions or equivalent)
CLAUDE.md created with project context and domain model summary
advance_criteria: Framework dev server starts with no errors
`npm run build` or equivalent exits 0
Database connection verified from application code
TypeScript compiles clean (zero errors)
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Core Schema
phases.purpose: Define all data models and run migrations before building features. Schema changes after features are built break existing code and data.

deliverables.text: All core tables/collections created via migrations
Relationships and constraints defined (foreign keys, unique indexes, not-null constraints)
ORM models or query layer set up (Drizzle, Prisma, or raw SQL with type wrappers)
Seed script for local development data
Migration strategy documented (how to run, how to rollback)

advance_criteria: All migrations run cleanly from scratch on a fresh database
Seed script creates enough data to develop against
ORM types match the domain model from Phase 0
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Design
phases.purpose: Design the full user experience before building it. Every screen, every interaction, every state. Building without a spec produces inconsistent UX and requires constant rework.

deliverables.text: User flow: entry points → core actions → success states → error states for each role
Page/screen inventory with purpose and key interactions
Component hierarchy (which components compose into which pages)

deliverables: Design tokens: brand colors, typography scale, spacing system, border radii
Navigation structure (sidebar, header, mobile nav)

deliverables.text: Empty states, loading states, and error states for each data-driven view
Form design: field layout, validation messaging, submission feedback

deliverables: Mobile layout decisions (responsive breakpoints, mobile-specific patterns)

deliverables.text: docs/product-development/ — product positioning documents that inform the design: product-story.md (target user, problem, core value proposition), product-synthesis.md (north star positioning document synthesizing story and strategy into a single agreed frame for product, design, and marketing). Seeded to project RAG.

design/wireframes/wireframes.html — self-contained wireframe file covering every planned screen, built from the project's design tokens; navigable in a browser and used to discuss layout, unique affordances, and interaction patterns before any implementation begins

advance_criteria: Every page that will be built is named and its purpose described
Empty, loading, and error states are designed for every list/data view
Mobile layout is explicitly planned (not assumed to 'just work')
Design tokens committed to project config (Tailwind theme extension or CSS variables)

docs/product-development/product-synthesis.md agreed by human as the north star positioning document — competitive position, target buyer, value chain, and AI/voice/integration stance confirmed before wireframes are finalized
design/wireframes/wireframes.html created and covers every planned screen — layout, affordances, and interaction patterns reviewed and agreed before feature implementation starts

phases.name: Core Features
phases.purpose: Build the primary feature set from the design spec. One feature at a time, fully complete (API + UI + validation + error states) before starting the next.
deliverables: All core CRUD operations implemented (create, read, update, delete for primary entities)
API endpoints with Zod/schema validation on all inputs
UI pages matching the design spec
Form validation with user-facing error messages
Loading and empty states implemented (not left as TODOs)
Data fetching pattern established and consistent across pages
advance_criteria: All core features work end-to-end on happy path
Form validation catches and shows errors (not just server-side)
No unhandled loading states (spinners or skeletons in place)
API inputs validated — bad data returns 400, not 500
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Auth & Authorization
phases.purpose: Add authentication and role-based access control. Auth touches every layer of the stack — doing it after features creates security gaps and requires retroactive middleware work.
deliverables: Auth provider integrated (Clerk, NextAuth/Auth.js, Lucia, or custom)
Sign in / sign up / sign out flows working
Protected routes — unauthorized access redirects to login
Session management (JWT, cookie, or server session — documented decision)
Role-based access: permissions enforced server-side, not just in UI
User profile and account management page
Password reset flow (if using credential auth)
advance_criteria: Unauthenticated requests to protected routes get 401/redirect (not 500 or 200)
Role permissions enforced at API layer (not just hidden in UI)
Auth state persists across page refresh
Sign up → onboarding → core feature flow works end-to-end
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Testing
phases.purpose: Write tests that catch real regressions — not tests that just execute code. Test the critical paths and domain invariants, not every getter and setter.
deliverables: Unit tests for all pure functions and domain logic
Integration tests for critical API routes (happy path + validation errors + auth checks)
Component tests for complex interactive components
E2E test for the primary user flow (signup → core action → success state)
Test database configured (isolated from dev data)
CI runs the test suite on every push
advance_criteria: `npm test` passes with zero failures
CI runs tests on push and blocks merge on failure
Critical API routes have auth tests (verifies 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for wrong role)
Primary user flow covered by at least one E2E test
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Polish
phases.purpose: Harden the app for real users — performance, accessibility, mobile, and production configuration.
deliverables: Mobile audit: all pages tested at 375px and 768px breakpoints
Accessibility audit: keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, color contrast
Lighthouse Performance ≥ 85 on primary pages
Production environment config: env vars set, secrets managed, debug logging off
Error boundaries in place (app doesn't white-screen on unexpected errors)
Rate limiting on auth endpoints and any public-facing mutation routes
CORS configuration locked down for production
Content Security Policy headers set
advance_criteria: All pages usable at 375px (no horizontal scroll, no overlapping elements)
No Lighthouse Accessibility violations (red flags)
Production env vars documented and set in deployment environment
Auth endpoints have rate limiting in place
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Extract
phases.purpose: Capture what was learned — patterns, architectural decisions, and reusable components — back into the workbench RAG and skill files.
deliverables: Session postmortem written and ingested to project RAG
Novel patterns captured as skill files (anything that took meaningful effort to figure out)
Architectural decisions documented (why this auth provider, why this data fetching approach, etc.)
Component library documented if substantial
advance_criteria: Postmortem ingested to RAG
Any decision that took real time to reach is documented

phases.name: QA Gate
phases.purpose: Human-verified test of the full application before launch prep begins.
deliverables: All primary user flows tested by a human (not just automated tests)
Mobile verified on a real device (not just browser DevTools responsive mode)
Auth flows verified: sign up, sign in, sign out, protected route access denied
Error states verified: form validation, API error messages, network failure handling
Test suite passing in CI
advance_criteria: Human has clicked through all primary flows (not delegated to automated tests)
Mobile verified on a physical device
Zero known bugs that block primary flows

phases.name: Support Audit
phases.purpose: Inventory every error state and user-facing failure before launch so support issues are handled by design.
deliverables: Error state inventory: what can go wrong, at what point in the flow
Support scenario table: scenario → likely cause → customer-facing message → resolution
High-risk edge cases identified and handled or documented
advance_criteria: Every form has user-facing validation messages (not raw error codes)
API errors return structured, human-readable messages (not stack traces)
Support scenario table committed to project docs
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Support Automation
phases.purpose: Reduce inbound support volume with self-serve tooling and hardened error messaging.
deliverables: FAQ or help documentation page
All error messages reviewed for clarity (specific, actionable, not 'Something went wrong')
Account self-service: password reset, email change, account deletion
support-playbook.md: internal runbook for common support tickets
advance_criteria: Help/FAQ page exists and is linked from the app
All error messages specific and actionable
Account self-service flows work end-to-end
/phase-audit run — findings addressed or deferred with ponytail: comments

phases.name: Infrastructure
deliverables: Hosting provisioned (Vercel, Railway, Fly.io, or cloud provider)
Production database provisioned and connection string set
Domain configured and pointing to deployment
All env vars set in production environment
CDN configured for static assets
advance_criteria: Production URL returns 200
Database connection from production verified
TypeScript build succeeds on production deployment

phases.name: Staging & Smoke Test
phases.purpose: Verify the full application against the production environment before opening to users.
deliverables: Full sign up → core action → success flow on production URL
Auth flows verified (sign in, sign out, protected route)
Database writes and reads verified against production database
Email delivery verified (if applicable)
advance_criteria: Primary flow works on production URL
No 500 errors in production logs during smoke test

phases.name: Legal & Compliance
phases.purpose: Legal minimum for a live web application.
deliverables: /privacy — Privacy Policy
/terms — Terms of Service
Cookie consent (if using analytics or third-party tracking)
GDPR/CCPA compliance basics if collecting personal data
advance_criteria: Privacy and Terms pages live and linked in footer
Cookie consent functional before any tracking scripts load

phases.name: Brand & Identity Finalization
phases.purpose: Finalize the product's brand identity before launch. The product is now fully built — you know what it actually is, what surprised you, and what users responded to. The name, story, and visual language decided in Phase 0 were hypotheses. This phase confirms or refines them with complete knowledge. No launch proceeds until the brand package is explicitly approved.
deliverables: Product name confirmed — domain available, App Store/Play Store slot open, trademark checked, social handles reserved
docs/product-development/product-story.md — final version rewritten with post-build knowledge; Phase 0 draft preserved as reference section
docs/product-development/brand-identity.md — one-liner, tagline, brand values (3–5 words), voice and tone guide
Color palette finalized — primary, secondary, accent, background, error, text roles; hex codes documented; WCAG AA contrast verified
Typography confirmed — primary and body fonts, weights, size scale, fallback stack; font license documented
Logo delivered — SVG source files: mark, wordmark, full logo in light and dark variants; PNG exports at all required sizes
App icon / favicon generated from final logomark at all required platform sizes
Domain registered and SSL configured
Launch copy drafted — App Store / Play Store description (short and long), keywords, tagline for Product Hunt or launch post, landing page hero copy
advance_criteria: Product name is final — agreed by all stakeholders, not a working title
docs/product-development/product-story.md updated with full post-build knowledge
docs/product-development/brand-identity.md complete — one-liner, tagline, brand values, voice guide, colors, typography all documented
Logo delivered as SVG source files (not PNG only) in light and dark variants
WCAG AA contrast verified for primary text on background color
Domain registered and SSL certificate provisioned
Human explicitly approves the brand package before launch proceeds

phases.name: Monitoring Setup
phases.purpose: Know immediately when something breaks in production.
deliverables: Error tracking configured (Sentry or equivalent)
Uptime monitoring configured
Application logs accessible (not just console.log in serverless limbo)
Performance baseline captured (Core Web Vitals on primary pages)
advance_criteria: Test error shows up in Sentry
Uptime monitor pinging production URL

phases.name: Go Live
phases.purpose: Open to real users and verify the first real session.
deliverables: App announced (social, email list, Product Hunt if applicable)
First real user completes the primary flow
No Sentry errors from first hour of real traffic
First real session reviewed in analytics
advance_criteria: At least one real user has completed the primary flow
No unhandled errors in first hour of traffic

phases.name: Ongoing
phases.purpose: Sustain and improve the application after launch.
deliverables: Weekly: review Sentry for new errors, address any critical issues
Monthly: review Core Web Vitals, check for dependency updates
Feature additions follow the same Phase 0 → Design → Build → Test → Extract process
Database migrations tested against production data before applying

milestones.label: Build complete — hand off to human for launch

roadmap:
0. Planning & DDD: event-storming → define-bounded-contexts → design-aggregates → model-domain-events → ubiquitous-language (run before writing any code)
1. Scaffold: framework, TypeScript, CI, database connection
2. Core Schema: migrations, ORM models, seed data
D. Design: user flows, page inventory, component hierarchy, design tokens, mobile plan
3. Core Features: CRUD, API validation, UI, loading/error states
4. Auth: provider integration, protected routes, role enforcement
5. Testing: unit, integration, E2E for critical paths
6. Polish: mobile audit, a11y, performance, production config
7. Extract: RAG ingest, skill files, decisions
8. QA Gate: human-verified full feature test
9. Support Audit: error state inventory
10. Support Automation: FAQ, error messages, playbook
[Milestone A — hand off to human]
11. Infrastructure: hosting, domain, env vars
12. Staging & Smoke Test
13. Legal & Compliance
14. Monitoring Setup
15. Go Live
[Milestone B — ongoing]
16. Ongoing: weekly/monthly cadence
